question_bank.stem: For Atari Breakout, the DQN maps the screen state to what output structure?

options.text: A probability distribution over all brick layouts
A reconstruction of the next video frame
A vector of Q-values for available actions

question_bank.rationale: The Q-network's outputs are action values such as right, left, or idle, not a score or reconstructed image.

distractor_rationales.A: DQN predicts action values during play, not only a final win/loss label.
distractor_rationales.B: The output indexes actions rather than possible layouts.
distractor_rationales.C: Frame prediction is not the DQN objective shown in the lecture.

source_ref.evidence_span: it will be the Q values associated

frame_evidence.description: Breakout preprocessing slide shows the game screen, input to the Q-network, and output Q-values for actions.

question_bank.stem: In Breakout preprocessing, removing the score is reasonable in the lecture's setup because the score provides what kind of information for paddle control?

options.text: Motion information needed to infer ball velocity
Little strategy information for deciding the next move
The only reward signal used for Bellman targets
A replacement for the action-value output layer

question_bank.rationale: The instructor argues the score can be removed because it does not matter for the local Breakout strategy being learned.

distractor_rationales.A: Motion comes from frame history, not from the score display.
distractor_rationales.C: Reward is part of the environment feedback, not read as pixels from the score here.
distractor_rationales.D: The score cannot replace the Q-values for actions.

frame_evidence.description: Breakout application slide shows preprocessing steps before a convolutional Q-network and a linear Q-value output.

question_bank.stem: Stacking several recent Breakout frames helps the Q-network infer what property that a single still screen can hide?

options.text: The score font at the top

question_bank.rationale: A short history of screens provides temporal information, allowing the network to infer velocity and direction.

distractor_rationales.A: Final outcome is not directly visible from a small frame stack.
distractor_rationales.B: The score is cropped because it is not central to paddle strategy.
distractor_rationales.D: Frame history describes input preprocessing, not model depth.

frame_evidence.description: Breakout application slide shows preprocessing steps before a convolutional Q-network and a linear Q-value output.

question_bank.stem: After Breakout screen preprocessing, the lecture uses what neural architecture family before producing linear Q-value outputs?

options.text: A convolutional neural network with ReLU activations
A recurrent language model with token embeddings
A tabular matrix indexed by state and action
A nearest-neighbor lookup over old screenshots

question_bank.rationale: The DQN architecture shown for images is a CNN with convolutional layers and ReLU activations followed by action-value outputs.

distractor_rationales.B: Language models are discussed later in RLHF, not for Breakout pixels.
distractor_rationales.C: The tabular matrix is what deep Q-learning avoids for large visual states.
distractor_rationales.D: The method learns a neural Q-function rather than nearest-neighbor retrieval.

source_ref.evidence_span: is going to be a convolutional neural network.
